title: BUG: wrong value returned by backend vs frontend, when a widget is rendered after a previous page run set a default value in session state
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

If a default value is set in session state on one page run, and then subsequently a widget is rendered with a corresponding `key`, then the default value is not picked up properly and the frontend and backend show different values for that widget.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# Sets default on first page run
st.session_state.setdefault("foo", 100.0)

if st.toggle("Show"):
    foo = st.number_input("Foo", key="foo")  # Shows 0.00
    st.write("You entered:", foo)  # Shows 100.0
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1.Turn on the  toggle
2. Compare the value in the widget vs the value printed underneath

### Expected Behavior

The value in the widget should match the number reported underneath.

### Current Behavior

The input widget displays `0.00`, but the backend reports `You entered: 100`.

If `r` is pressed to trigger a re-run, then the frontend updates to display `0.0` and the default value is lost.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

This bug is problematic for more complex pages, where widgets may need to be "loaded" or "reset" programmatically, and some widgets may be conditionally hidden depending on a toggle or checkbox.

The bug does not happen if `persist_state="page"` is passed to `number_input`.

Possibly related: #15660 seems to have fixed a similar bug for when persist_state is passed, but not for when persist_state=None.

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17093)

When a keyed widget is first rendered on a later run than the one that wrote its `st.session_state` default (e.g. `setdefault` while the widget is hidden behind a toggle), the backend returns that stored value but the frontend mounts at the widget element default. A follow-up rerun then writes the frontend default back into session state, so the programmatic value is lost. Root cause: `SessionState.register_widget` only sets `value_changed=True` for same-run assignments (`is_new_state_value`) or for `persist_state` remounts (`restored_persisted_value` from PR #15660). For `persist_state=None`, a previous-run user-key value in `_old_state` is resolved on the Python side but never sent via `set_value`, so `st.number_input` (and other widgets) render `0.00` / empty while returning `100.0`. Passing `persist_state="page"` works because that path already tells the frontend to adopt the backend value.

### Related Issues

- [#5620](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5620) — Likely duplicate: a keyed `st.text_input` revealed by a checkbox does not load a `session_state` value set on a prior run.
- [#9082](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9082) — Same `setdefault` + conditional-widget pattern; the first-rendered widget gets the default, later-revealed widgets do not, and hiding them can clear session state.
- [#16388](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16388) — Related frontend/backend split for keyed widgets, but triggered by deleting a session-state key rather than delayed first mount.
